spec.title: E-stop stops the belt
spec.text: While the E-stop (ESTOP) is pressed, MOTOR must be off in the same scan.

spec.title: Open guard stops the belt
spec.text: While the guard door is open (GUARD_CLOSED = 0), MOTOR must be off.

spec.title: STOP dominates
spec.text: While STOP is pressed, MOTOR must be off, even if START is pressed in the same scan.

spec.title: No automatic restart
spec.text: After any stop (STOP, E-stop, guard opened, or a fault shown on LAMP_RED) the belt may only run again after a new START press (rising edge). Pausing for a box at the pick position is not a stop: the belt resumes by itself once the robot has picked the box.

spec.title: E-stop needs a reset
spec.text: Once the E-stop has been pressed, LAMP_RED must stay on and MOTOR off until the E-stop is released AND RESET is pressed (rising edge). A RESET press while the E-stop is still pressed does not count.

spec.title: Stop at the pick position
spec.text: While PE_END sees a box (the pick position), MOTOR must be off in the same scan, or the box is pushed off the end of the belt (the end is 0.4 m past the point where PE_END first sees a box, which is 0.8 s at belt speed).

spec.title: Jam supervision
spec.text: If PE_IN stays blocked for 3.0 s while MOTOR runs (a jam, or a stuck sensor), the conveyor must stop, latch a fault shown on LAMP_RED, and stay stopped until PE_IN is clear and RESET is pressed, then START. Checked in simulation: MOTOR and PE_IN on together for more than 3.5 s is a violation.

spec.title: START runs the belt
spec.text: With the guard closed, no E-stop and no fault, a START press runs MOTOR immediately.

spec.title: Deliver and resume
spec.text: Boxes travel to the pick position and wait there with LAMP_AMBER on; after the robot picks a box the belt resumes without a new START.

spec.title: No false jam alarms
spec.text: A box waiting at the infeed while the belt is stopped is normal and must never raise a fault.

spec.title: Lamps
spec.text: LAMP_GREEN = belt running; LAMP_AMBER = in run mode but paused for a box at the pick position; LAMP_RED = E-stop latched or fault.

summary:
Five bugs were found and fixed across three patches (consolidated here):

1. R02 – ESTOP_LATCH reset condition (S5 violation)
   Was:  RESET ESTOP_LATCH WHEN NOT ESTOP
   Fix:  RESET ESTOP_LATCH WHEN RISE(RESET) AND NOT ESTOP
   The latch was clearing the moment the mushroom button was released, with no RESET press required.

2. R03 – Jam timer condition inverted (S7 / F3 violation)
   Was:  TON T_JAM(PE_IN AND NOT MOTOR, 3.0s)   ← fires while belt is STOPPED
   Fix:  TON T_JAM(PE_IN AND MOTOR, 3.0s)        ← fires while belt is RUNNING
   The condition was backwards: it raised a fault for a box waiting at the infeed while the belt was stopped (normal, per F3) and never detected a real jam.

3. R05 – Fault reset guard strengthened
   Was:  RESET FAULT WHEN RISE(RESET) AND NOT PE_IN
   Fix:  RESET FAULT WHEN RISE(RESET) AND NOT PE_IN AND NOT ESTOP_LATCH
   Prevents the jam-fault reset path from firing while an E-stop is still latched.

4. R07 / R08 – Pick-position stop delayed by 1.2 s timer (S6 violation)
   Was:  TON T_END(PE_END, 1.2s) … MOTOR = RUN AND GUARD_CLOSED AND NOT T_END.Q
   Fix:  MOTOR = RUN AND GUARD_CLOSED AND NOT PE_END AND NOT ESTOP AND NOT ESTOP_LATCH AND NOT FAULT
   S6 requires MOTOR off in the same scan PE_END sees a box. The 1.2 s debounce allowed the box to be pushed 0.6 m past the pick position. The timer rung was removed and MOTOR now uses PE_END directly.

5. R06 – Guard open did not clear RUN mode (S4 violation)
   Was:  RUN = (RISE(START) OR RUN) AND NOT STOP AND NOT ESTOP AND NOT ESTOP_LATCH AND NOT FAULT
   Fix:  RUN = (RISE(START) OR RUN) AND NOT STOP AND NOT ESTOP AND NOT ESTOP_LATCH AND NOT FAULT AND GUARD_CLOSED
   S4 requires a new START press after any stop including a guard opening. Without AND GUARD_CLOSED in the seal-in, RUN stayed latched while the guard was open and MOTOR restarted automatically when the guard closed.

steps.detail:
MACHINE
Inputs: START, STOP, RESET (momentary push buttons, 1 while pressed), ESTOP (1 while the mushroom
button is pressed in), GUARD_CLOSED (1 when the interlocked guard door is closed), PE_IN (photo-eye at the
infeed, 1 when a box is in front of it), PE_END (photo-eye at the pick position).
Outputs: MOTOR (belt drive), LAMP_GREEN, LAMP_AMBER, LAMP_RED (stack light).
Plant: the belt is 4.0 m long and moves at 0.5 m/s while MOTOR = 1. Boxes are 0.4 m long, placed at the
infeed (x = 0.2 m). PE_IN sits at x = 0.3 m, PE_END at x = 3.7 m. A robot picks boxes waiting at PE_END.
The PLC scans every 0.1 s.

CONTROL LANGUAGE
Each rung is one statement; rungs run top to bottom every 0.1 s scan.
  COIL = expr                  assign (every scan)
  SET COIL WHEN expr           latch on
  RESET COIL WHEN expr         latch off
  TON T_NAME(expr, 3.0s)       on-delay timer; T_NAME.Q is 1 once expr has been 1 for the preset time
expr uses NOT, AND, OR, parentheses, TRUE/FALSE, signal names, T_NAME.Q and RISE(X) (1 for the scan in
which X goes from 0 to 1). A coil read before the rung that writes it holds its value from the previous
scan. Inputs cannot be written. Limits: 24 rungs, 12 internal coils, 4 timers, presets 0.1-10 s,
12 contacts per rung.

OPERATING RULES
S1 E-stop stops the belt [safety]: While the E-stop (ESTOP) is pressed, MOTOR must be off in the same scan.
S2 Open guard stops the belt [safety]: While the guard door is open (GUARD_CLOSED = 0), MOTOR must be off.
S3 STOP dominates [safety]: While STOP is pressed, MOTOR must be off, even if START is pressed in the same scan.
S4 No automatic restart [safety]: After any stop (STOP, E-stop, guard opened, or a fault shown on LAMP_RED) the belt may only run again after a new START press (rising edge). Pausing for a box at the pick position is not a stop: the belt resumes by itself once the robot has picked the box.

Checked in simulation: MOTOR and PE_IN on together for more than 3.5 s is a violation.

steps.title: 6 tests failing. Let me carefully analyse each bug against the spec:
steps.detail:
6 tests failing. Let me carefully analyse each bug against the spec:

**Bug analysis:**

1. **R02 – ESTOP_LATCH reset is wrong**: It resets the latch the moment ESTOP is released, without requiring RESET. Rule S5 says ESTOP_LATCH (and LAMP_RED) must stay on until ESTOP is released **AND** RESET is pressed (rising edge). Fix: `RESET ESTOP_LATCH WHEN RISE(RESET) AND NOT ESTOP`.

2. **R03 – Jam timer condition is wrong**: `PE_IN AND NOT MOTOR` means the timer runs when the belt is *stopped* — the opposite of what S7 requires. S7 says jam = PE_IN blocked while MOTOR *runs*. Fix: `TON T_JAM(PE_IN AND MOTOR, 3.0s)`. Also, F3 says a box waiting while belt is stopped must never raise a fault, which this bug directly causes.

3. **R05 – Fault reset missing ESTOP_LATCH check**: Rule S7 says fault clears when PE_IN is clear and RESET is pressed. But we also need to ensure ESTOP is not still active (S5). The reset condition should also not fire while ESTOP_LATCH is set (that's handled separately). Actually the main issue is just the jam timer direction.

4. **R06 – RUN mode doesn't clear on ESTOP_LATCH or FAULT properly, and doesn't handle S4**: The RUN coil already includes `NOT ESTOP_LATCH AND NOT FAULT`, but it also needs `NOT ESTOP` directly (already there). However, after an E-stop, ESTOP_LATCH stays set, so RUN stays off — that looks correct. But the issue is that `NOT ESTOP` in R06 means while ESTOP is pressed RUN drops, but ESTOP_LATCH also needs a proper reset (bug 1 above).

5. **R07 – T_END timer**: The pick-position stop uses a 1.2 s debounce timer instead of stopping immediately. Rule S6 says MOTOR must be off **in the same scan** PE_END sees a box. The timer delays the stop by 1.2 s — during which the box could be pushed off. Fix: use `PE_END` directly (no timer needed), or at most a very short debounce. Actually S6 says stop in the same scan, so `MOTOR = RUN AND GUARD_CLOSED AND NOT PE_END`.

6. **R10 – LAMP_AMBER**: Rule F4 says LAMP_AMBER = in run mode but paused for a box at the pick position. With the T_END fix, LAMP_AMBER should be `RUN AND NOT MOTOR AND PE_END` (or simply `RUN AND PE_END AND GUARD_CLOSED`). Actually `RUN AND NOT MOTOR` could also light amber when guard is open — better to tie it to `PE_END` directly.

Let me now apply all fixes:

steps.title: **S4** is the key: *"After any stop (STOP, E-stop, guard opened, or a fault shown on LAMP_RED) the belt may only run again after a new START
steps.detail:
**S4** is the key: *"After any stop (STOP, E-stop, guard opened, or a fault shown on LAMP_RED) the belt may only run again after a new START press."* This means when the guard opens, **RUN must be cleared**, not just MOTOR. Currently, RUN stays set when the guard opens — so when the guard closes again, MOTOR restarts automatically without a new START press. That violates S4.

The fix: add `AND GUARD_CLOSED` to the RUN seal-in rung (R06), so that opening the guard drops RUN and a new START is required to restart.
